analyst_view.overall: Atalanta (12th, 14 pts, one win in five) host second-placed Inter (28 pts, four wins in five) after the international break, with Sarri's side well short of last season's level and Chivu's Inter chasing the top spot. Inter's attack is thin: Lautaro Martinez is back in group training after a hamstring strain since 13 October and may start, Thuram came home from France duty with fatigue and is day to day, Bonny is out about three more weeks and Esposito is being checked; none of this is in the numbers, which list no missing players. Atalanta expect Raspadori, Kristensen, Bellanova and Gaetano back (maybe not for full minutes), while centre-backs Hien and Kossounou were still not reported fit. Inter host Stuttgart in the Champions League three days later and Chivu plans to share minutes between Lautaro and Thuram. One fixture site listed Calhanoglu as suspended, but the official matchday 12 suspension and booking-warning list (17 Nov) has no Inter or Atalanta player, so I treat him as available; no referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.0 of them for Inter. I lean mildly lower to about 2.9: Inter arrive with a patched-up attack (Lautaro just back after five weeks out, Thuram doubtful with fatigue, Bonny out) and Chivu plans to split minutes between his strikers before the Stuttgart game. Atalanta's leaky recent defence (12 conceded in six) is already in the numbers through momentum, so I don't count it again.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, with Inter's recent rise in corners (36 in six) and Atalanta conceding many already counted through momentum. Atalanta's wing-backs Bellanova and Kristensen returning should help them push wide at home, while Inter's thinner attack points the other way, so nothing clearly moves it; I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards and already add for the past meetings (head-to-head +13% on Atalanta's side) and for Atalanta's recent cards against. No referee has been named yet and neither side has anyone on a booking warning, so I find nothing the numbers miss and stay at 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, with Inter on 16.3 after a +10% momentum boost for their recent shooting. I trim slightly to about 27.9 because Inter's front line is short of fitness (Lautaro returning, Thuram doubtful, Bonny out) and minutes are likely to be managed before the Champions League; Atalanta getting Raspadori back is a small offset.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, 5.4 of them Inter's. For the same reason as goals, a rusty Lautaro and a doubtful Thuram with Bonny out, I lean mildly lower to about 8.9; Atalanta conceding plenty lately is already in the numbers.
